bloques.titulo: Essential contrast between niet and geen
texto: The gold rule of denial in Dutch is: «geen» is used to deny nouns preceded by an undetermined article («een») or without any article: «Ik drink geen koffie» (I don't drink coffee), «Ik heb geen suiker» (I don't have sugar). For everything else (verbs, adjectives, adverbs, own or substantive names with specific article «de/het»), «niet»: «De winkel is niet open» (the store is not open), «Ik werk vandaag niet» (today I do not work) is used.

analisis: No coffee; I don't drink coffee

frases.nl: Ik heb geen suiker, maar wel melk.
frases.es: No tengo azúcar, pero sí leche.
frases.en: I don't have sugar, but I do have milk.

frases.nl: Mijn broer is vandaag niet thuis.
frases.es: Mi hermano no está en casa hoy.

frases.nl: Wij werken vandaag niet; we zijn vrij.
frases.es: Hoy no trabajamos; tenemos el día libre.
frases.en: We don't work today; we have the day off.
analisis: We are free; we have the day free

bloques.pregunta: When should «geen» be used instead of «niet»?

opciones.texto: Para negar sustantivos sin artículo determinado o que llevarían «een»
opciones.explicacion: It equals «No / no of / no» to an indefinite noun.

opciones.texto: Para negar adjetivos calificativos en cualquier posición
opciones.explicacion: Adjectives are always denied with «niet» («niet open», «niet mooi»).

opciones.texto: Exclusively at the end of the interrogation sentences
opciones.explicacion: The position of «geen» depends on the noun to which it accompanies, not the type of sentence.

bloques.pregunta: What does the person have and what does he lack?
bloques.frase: Ik heb geen suiker, maar wel melk.

opciones.texto: He's got no sugar, but he's got milk.
opciones.explicacion: «Geen suiker» denies sugar and «wel melk» claims the presence of milk in contrast.

opciones.texto: It has plenty of sugar but it has no milk.
It lacks both sugar and milk.
opciones.explicacion: «Wel» introduces a statement that compensates for the previous deficiency.

bloques.pregunta: Complete with the right denial particle for an adjective.

opciones.explicacion: Qualitative adjectives are necessarily denied with «niet», never with «geen».
«Geen» only accompanies indeterminate nouns, not adjectives like «open».
Although grammatical, «wel» would say that it is open, the opposite of denial.

bloques.pregunta: Why don't you work on the text today?
bloques.frase: Wij werken vandaag niet; we zijn vrij.

opciones.texto: Because today they have the day off.
opciones.explicacion: «We zijn vrij» means they are free from work.

opciones.texto: Because the office is closed for failure.
opciones.explicacion: He does not mention any fault, but they enjoy his day off.

opciones.texto: Because they have to go to a class in Utrecht.
opciones.explicacion: He is not talking about Dutch classes, but about work rest.

bloques.pregunta: Complete the denial to the non-accounting common noun «koffie».

opciones.explicacion: «geen» is required to be used in the face of a substantive without a particular article.
With an indeterminate noun, «niet» is not used, but «geen».
It would express a strong statement («I do.»), contrary to negative intention.

bloques.explicacion: Initial warning with verbal investment and negative particle «geen» to the noun.

intro: Distinguish precisely when to deny with geen (indeterminate nouns) and with niet (verbs, adjectives and defined elements).
